GDMA Master Receive Slave Transmit

This sample demonstrates communication between an I2C master device and a slave device using GDMA. Meanwhile, the master and the slave are interconnected to achieve transmission that master transmit data and slave receive data.

The master device acts as the receiver, using two GDMA channels to send read command and receive data; the slave device acts as the sender, using GDMA for transmit data.

In this sample, I2C0 is configured as the master device; I2C1 is configured as the slave device.

Requirements

For requirements, please refer to the Requirements.

Wiring

Connect P4_0 (master SCL) to P4_2 (slave SCL), P4_1 (master SDA) to P4_3 (slave SDA) on the EVB.

Note

The frequency of SCL is influenced by both the pull-up resistor and the wire capacitance. Therefore, it is strongly recommended to choose appropriate pull-up resistors to make the frequency accurate. This sample need connect 2.2 kΩ pull-up resistors.

The connection schematic of the pull-up resistor is shown below:

Configurations

  1. The following macros can be configured to modify pin definitions.

    #define I2C0_SCL_PIN                         P4_0
#define I2C0_SDA_PIN                         P4_1

#define I2C1_SCL_PIN                         P4_2
#define I2C1_SDA_PIN                         P4_3

  2. The following macros can be configured to modify the GDMA TX and GDMA RX channel settings.

    // Set the folling macros to modify the I2C0 RX GDMA Channel configurations.
#define I2C0_GDMA_CHANNEL_NUM                 0
#define I2C0_GDMA_Channel                     GDMA_Channel0
#define I2C0_GDMA_Channel_IRQn                GDMA0_Channel0_IRQn
#define I2C0_GDMA_Channel_Handler             GDMA0_Channel0_Handler

// Set the folling macros to modify the I2C1 TX GDMA Channel configurations.
#define I2C1_GDMA_CHANNEL_NUM                 1
#define I2C1_GDMA_Channel                     GDMA_Channel1
#define I2C1_GDMA_Channel_IRQn                GDMA0_Channel1_IRQn
#define I2C1_GDMA_Channel_Handler             GDMA0_Channel1_Handler

// Set the folling macros to modify the I2C0 TX GDMA Channel configurations.
#define I2C0_READ_CMD_GDMA_CHANNEL_NUM        2
#define I2C0_READ_CMD_GDMA_Channel            GDMA_Channel2
#define I2C0_READ_CMD_GDMA_Channel_IRQn       GDMA0_Channel2_IRQn
#define I2C0_READ_CMD_GDMA_Channel_Handler    GDMA0_Channel2_Handler

  3. The following macros can be configured to modify the I2C GDMA data transfer length.

    #define GDMA_TRANSFER_SIZE                    200                      /*< Set this macro to modify the transfer size. */

Building and Downloading

For building and downloading, please refer to the Building and Downloading.

Experimental Verification

  1. When the EVB starts, GDMA channel 2 transfers the read command data to the master's TX FIFO. The master device sends a read request command to the slave device, and when completing the transmission, it enters the GDMA channel 2 interrupt and prints log.

    I2C0_READ_CMD_GDMA2_Channel_Handler!

  2. When the slave device receives a read request from the master device, the I2C_INT_RD_REQ interrupt is triggered which GDMA1 is enabled to transfer data in the interrupt handler. The slave device sends data to the master via GDMA channel 1. when completing the transmission, it enters the GDMA channel 1 interrupt and prints log.

    In I2C1_GDMA_Channel_Handler! I2C slave send data by GDMA successfully

  3. The Master receives the data sent by the Slave via GDMA channel 0, and when completing the transmission, it enters the GDMA channel 0 interrupt and prints the sent and received data.

    I2C0_GDMA_Channel_Handler!I2C master read data by GDMA successfully
GDMA_Send_Buf = 0, GDMA_Recv_Buf = 0
...
GDMA_Send_Buf = 199, GDMA_Recv_Buf = 199

Code Overview

This section introduces the code and process description for initialization and corresponding function implementation in the sample.

Source Code Directory

The directory for project file and source code are as follows:

  • Project directory: sdk\samples\peripheral\i2c\gdma_master_rx_slave_tx\proj

  • Source code directory: sdk\samples\peripheral\i2c\gdma_master_rx_slave_tx\src

Initialization

The initialization flow for peripherals can refer to Initialization Flow in General Introduction.

  1. Call Pad_Config() and Pinmux_Config() to configure the PAD and PINMUX of the corresponding pins.

    void board_i2c_master_init(void)
{
   Pad_Config(I2C_MASTER_SCL_PIN, PAD_PINMUX_MODE, PAD_IS_PWRON, PAD_PULL_UP, PAD_OUT_ENABLE, PAD_OUT_HIGH);
   Pad_Config(I2C_MASTER_SDA_PIN, PAD_PINMUX_MODE, PAD_IS_PWRON, PAD_PULL_UP, PAD_OUT_ENABLE, PAD_OUT_HIGH);

   Pinmux_Config(I2C_MASTER_SCL_PIN, I2C0_CLK);
   Pinmux_Config(I2C_MASTER_SDA_PIN, I2C0_DAT);
}

void board_i2c_slave_init(void)
{
   Pad_Config(I2C_SLAVE_SCL_PIN, PAD_PINMUX_MODE, PAD_IS_PWRON, PAD_PULL_UP, PAD_OUT_ENABLE, PAD_OUT_HIGH);
   Pad_Config(I2C_SLAVE_SDA_PIN, PAD_PINMUX_MODE, PAD_IS_PWRON, PAD_PULL_UP, PAD_OUT_ENABLE, PAD_OUT_HIGH);

   Pinmux_Config(I2C_SLAVE_SCL_PIN, I2C1_CLK);
   Pinmux_Config(I2C_SLAVE_SDA_PIN, I2C1_DAT);
}

  2. Call RCC_PeriphClockCmd() to enable the I2C clock.

  3. Initialize the I2C peripheral:

    1. Define the I2C_InitTypeDef type I2C_InitStruct, and call I2C_StructInit() to pre-fill I2C_InitStruct with default values.

    2. Modify the I2C_InitStruct parameters as needed. The initialization parameter configurations for I2C0 and I2C1 are shown in the table below. Call I2C_Init() to initialize the I2C peripheral.

  2. Configure I2C1 read request interrupt: I2C_INT_RD_REQ and NVIC. For NVIC configuration, refer to Interrupt Configuration.

6. Initialize I2C0 (master) GDMA TX data information, and initialize I2C1 (slave) GDMA TX data information. Setting BIT8 of the data to 1 represents a Master Read operation, and setting BIT9 to 1 represents the Master sending a stop bit.

/* Initialize data buffer */
for (uint32_t i = 0; i < (GDMA_TRANSFER_SIZE - 1); i++)
{
    GDMA_I2C_Tx_Read_Buf[i] = (0x01 << 8);
}
GDMA_I2C_Tx_Read_Buf[GDMA_TRANSFER_SIZE - 1] = (0x03 << 8);

  1. Initialize the GDMA peripheral:

    1. Define a GDMA_InitTypeDef type GDMA_InitStruct, and call GDMA_StructInit() to pre-fill GDMA_InitStruct with default values.

    2. Modify the GDMA_InitStruct parameters as needed. The initialization parameters for the GDMA TX and RX channels are configured as shown in the table below. Call GDMA_Init() to initialize the GDMA peripheral.

    3. Configure the GDMA total transfer complete interrupt GDMA_INT_Transfer and NVIC. For NVIC configuration, refer to Interrupt Configuration.

Functional Implementation

The master device receives the transmission from the slave device using the GDMA transfer process as shown in the figure:

  1. After enabling the master device GDMA TX transmission channel, the GDMA TX channel transfers data from GDMA_I2C_Tx_Read_Buf to (&(I2C0->IC_DATA_CMD)), and the I2C master device begins sending read command data.

  2. When the I2C slave device receives the read request command from the master device, it triggers the I2C slave device I2C_INT_RD_REQ interrupt. Within the slave device interrupt function, call GDMA_Cmd() to enable the slave device GDMA channel 1 for sending, and the slave device begins transmitting data.

    void I2C1_Handler(void)
{
    if (I2C_GetINTStatus(I2C1, I2C_INT_RD_REQ) == SET)
    {
        GDMA_Cmd(I2C1_GDMA_CHANNEL_NUM, ENABLE);
        //Add user code here
        /* Clear interrupt */
        I2C_ClearINTPendingBit(I2C1, I2C_INT_RD_REQ);
        I2C_INTConfig(I2C1, I2C_INT_RD_REQ, DISABLE);
    }
}

  3. When the master device completes data transmission, it triggers the GDMA_INT_Transfer interrupt, and the corresponding information is printed within the interrupt handler function.

    void I2C0_READ_CMD_GDMA_Channel_Handler(void)
{
    GDMA_INTConfig(I2C0_READ_CMD_GDMA_CHANNEL_NUM, GDMA_INT_Transfer, DISABLE);
    DBG_DIRECT("I2C0_READ_CMD_GDMA2_Channel_Handler!");
    GDMA_ClearINTPendingBit(I2C0_READ_CMD_GDMA_CHANNEL_NUM, GDMA_INT_Transfer);
}

  4. After enabling the slave device GDMA TX transmission channel, the GDMA TX channel transfers data from GDMA_I2C_Send_Buf to (&(I2C1->IC_DATA_CMD)). When the GDMA TX data transmission is complete, it triggers the GDMA TX channel GDMA_INT_Transfer interrupt. The corresponding information is printed within the interrupt handler function.

    void I2C1_GDMA_Channel_Handler(void)
{
    GDMA_INTConfig(I2C1_GDMA_CHANNEL_NUM, GDMA_INT_Transfer, DISABLE);
    /* Notes: DBG_DIRECT is only used for debug demo, do not use in app!
        In app project, the APP_PRINT_INFO can be used.
    */
    DBG_DIRECT("In I2C1_GDMA_Channel_Handler! I2C slave send data by GDMA successfully");
    //Add user code here
    GDMA_ClearINTPendingBit(I2C1_GDMA_CHANNEL_NUM, GDMA_INT_Transfer);
}

  5. After enabling the main device GDMA RX transmission channel, the GDMA RX channel transfers data from (&(I2C0->IC_DATA_CMD)) to GDMA_I2C_Recv_Buf. When the GDMA RX data transmission is complete, it triggers the GDMA RX channel GDMA_INT_Transfer interrupt, and the corresponding information is printed within the interrupt handler function.

    void I2C0_GDMA_Channel_Handler(void)
{
    GDMA_INTConfig(I2C0_GDMA_CHANNEL_NUM, GDMA_INT_Transfer, DISABLE);
    DBG_DIRECT("I2C0_GDMA_Channel_Handler!I2C master read data by GDMA successfully");
    GDMA_ClearINTPendingBit(I2C0_GDMA_CHANNEL_NUM, GDMA_INT_Transfer);

    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < GDMA_TRANSFER_SIZE; i++)
    {
        if (GDMA_I2C_Send_Buf[i] != GDMA_I2C_Recv_Buf[i])
        {
            DBG_DIRECT(" Data transmission error! GDMA_Send_Buf = %d, GDMA_Recv_Buf = %d",
                    GDMA_I2C_Send_Buf[i], GDMA_I2C_Recv_Buf[i]);
        }
        DBG_DIRECT("GDMA_Send_Buf = %d, GDMA_Recv_Buf = %d",
                GDMA_I2C_Send_Buf[i], GDMA_I2C_Recv_Buf[i]);
        GDMA_I2C_Recv_Buf[i] = 0;
    }

}
